Finally, Paul urged believers, “Therefore encourage one another, and build each other up.” This shows us that a truly mature spiritual life is not only having faith, love, and hope ourselves, but being willing to help others grow together.

A self-centered life cares only about its own needs; a selfless life is willing to care for, support, and build up others. Faith makes us rely on God together, love makes us love one another, and hope makes us run toward eternity together. Life first, then relationships, then ministry. When we let Jesus live and be King within, we can build spiritual relationships of mutual encouragement and building up, and become victors who together welcome the Lord’s return.
a: Guard your life with faith and love
Do not let fear, pride, and selfish desire rule your heart. By the Spirit, live a life that trusts God and loves others.
Face life with eternal hope
Do not be discouraged by present difficulties and gains and losses. Remember Jesus’ salvation and prepare to welcome the Lord’s return.
Encourage one another and build each other up
Do not only pursue your own spiritual growth, but take the initiative to care for, encourage, and walk with others, living out Christ together.
q: Each day, am I controlled by circumstances, fear, and my own needs, or do I live in Christ with faith, love, and hope? Am I willing to be someone who encourages and builds up others?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for saving me through Jesus Christ, bringing me from darkness into light, and giving me eternal life and hope. Guard my heart, so that fear, pride, and selfish desire no longer rule it, but I live in Your light with faith and love. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus live in me and be King in me. Holy Spirit, guide my life. Help me hold on to the hope of salvation, so that I not only follow the Lord faithfully myself, but encourage and build up my brothers and sisters, live out the life of Christ together with them, and prepare to welcome the Lord’s return, giving all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I belong to the day! I will guard my life with faith and love, build others up with the hope of salvation, and live together with Christ!

t: Rely on God Together and Win the Battle Through the Lord
v: Then Amalek came and fought with Israel in Rephidim.
Moses said to Joshua, “Choose men for us, and go out to fight with Amalek. Tomorrow I will stand on the top of the hill with God’s rod in my hand.”
So Joshua did as Moses had told him, and fought with Amalek; and Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
When Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed. When he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.

But Moses’ hands were heavy; so they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side. His hands were steady until sunset.
Joshua defeated Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.
The LORD said to Moses, “Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: that I will utterly blot out the memory of Amalek from under the sky.”
Moses built an altar, and called its name “The LORD our Banner”.
He said, “The LORD has sworn: ‘The LORD will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.’”
b: In the wilderness the Israelites were attacked by the Amalekites. Moses told Joshua to lead the people out to fight, while he himself stood on top of the hill with the rod of God in his hand. When Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed; when he let his hand down, Amalek prevailed. True victory is not by human ability and strategy alone, but by relying on the God who commands the battle.

Joshua fulfilled his duty in the fight below, and Moses showed his reliance on God on the hill above; neither could be missing. We often think that with enough ability, experience, and resources we can overcome difficulties, forgetting that true strength comes from God. When we lay down self-centeredness, stop relying on our own cleverness, and let Jesus be King, we can experience God’s leading as we take responsible action.

Even though Moses was the leader God had chosen, his hands still grew weary, and Aaron and Hur had to hold them up on both sides. A true spiritual leader is not someone who is never weak, but someone willing to humbly accept help and complete God’s charge together with others.

A self-centered life likes to hold power alone and thinks it cannot be done without it; a selfless life is willing to work together and support one another. Aaron and Hur did not compete for Moses’ place, but faithfully supported him until his hands were steady until sunset. Life first, then relationships, then ministry. When we lay down pride and build relationships of spiritual companions who trust and complete one another, we can carry the mission in unity, so that God’s work does not stop because of one person’s limits.

Finally, after Israel’s victory, Moses built an altar and called it “Yahweh Nissi,” meaning “The LORD is my banner.” The key to victory is not who stands at the front, but who is lifted up highest. Moses did not give the glory to his own leadership or to Joshua’s bravery, but declared that the LORD was the banner of their victory.

The spiritual battle we face today is not a contest of winning and losing against people, but overcoming sin, pride, and self-centeredness through Christ. When we take Jesus as our Role Model, the Bible as our Standard, and the Holy Spirit as our Guide, and rely on God and hold one another up together, we can live out Christ’s victorious life and give all glory to him.
a: Rely on God in the battle
In difficulty, do not depend only on your own ability and methods, but pray and seek God while faithfully doing your part.
Humbly accept support and work together
Do not insist on carrying everything alone. Learn to hold one another up and complete one another, bearing God’s charge together.
Win through the Lord and give God the glory
Do not credit success to yourself. Exalt Jesus in everything and testify that he is the source of our victory.
q: In the difficulties and service I face, do I rely on my own ability and carry everything alone, or am I willing to humbly rely on God, support spiritual companions, and let Jesus be King?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for being my strength and the God who leads me to victory. When I face difficulty and battle, help me no longer rely on my own ability, but look to You alone. I am willing to lay down pride and self-centeredness and let Jesus live in me and be King in me. Holy Spirit, guide my life. Help me humbly accept help, support my spiritual companions and work with them, and faithfully complete Your charge. May I rely on Christ in everything and live a victorious life, declaring that You are my banner of victory, and give all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Yahweh Nissi! The LORD is my banner! I will rely on him with one heart and win the battle through the Lord!

t: Pour Out Your Heart to God, from Sorrow to Peace
v: So Hannah rose up after they had finished eating and drinking in Shiloh. Now Eli the priest was sitting on his seat by the doorpost of the LORD’s temple.
She was in bitterness of soul, and prayed to the LORD, weeping bitterly.

She vowed a vow, and said, “LORD of Armies, if you will indeed look at the affliction of your servant and remember me, and not forget your servant, but will give to your servant a boy, then I will give him to the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor shall come on his head.”
As she continued praying before the LORD, Eli saw her mouth.
Now Hannah spoke in her heart. Only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard. Therefore Eli thought she was drunk.
Eli said to her, “How long will you be drunk? Get rid of your wine!”
Hannah answered, “No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit. I have not been drinking wine or strong drink, but I poured out my soul before the LORD.
Don’t consider your servant a wicked woman; for I have been speaking out of the abundance of my complaint and my provocation.”
Then Eli answered, “Go in peace; and may the God of Israel grant your petition that you have asked of him.”
She said, “Let your servant find favor in your sight.” So the woman went her way and ate; and her facial expression wasn’t sad any more.
b: Because she could not have children, and was provoked by Peninnah, Hannah’s heart was full of pain and grief. She did not let sorrow drive her away from God, but came before the LORD and prayed with bitter weeping. True faith is not having no pain in the heart, but knowing to whom we can pour out our hearts in pain.

When people meet trouble, they often hide their hurt in their hearts or rush to find their own solutions; Hannah chose to bring her deepest wound before God. When we are no longer controlled by circumstances and others’ words, but turn our focus to God, we turn from relying on ourselves to relying on him, and learn to experience God’s comfort in weakness.

Hannah prayed without ceasing, and because her lips moved but her voice was not heard, the priest Eli mistook her for drunk. But she was not angry at being misunderstood; instead she humbly explained, “I am pouring out my soul before the LORD.” True prayer is not in how beautiful the words are, but in whether we sincerely bring our hearts before God.

Hannah asked God not only to give her a son, but was also willing to give the child she received back to God. This shows that in asking she was learning to entrust, wanting not only what she desired, but willing to let God use what she received. When we lay down self-centeredness and let God be God, we turn from clinging to our own needs to trusting God’s will.

Finally, Eli said to Hannah, “Go in peace.” Hannah went her way and ate, and her face was no longer sad. It is worth noting that Hannah’s circumstances had not changed, yet her heart had changed first. She had not yet conceived, nor seen the answer to her prayer, yet she had already moved from sorrow to peace.

True entrusting is not demanding that God change circumstances immediately, but being willing to place the outcome in his hands. When we let Jesus be King and by the Spirit hand our burdens to God, we are no longer bound by anxiety, we can still trust him while waiting, and we live a life of peace and hope.
a: Bring your sorrow to God
Do not let pain and grief pile up in your heart, but pour out your heart to God in prayer.
Do not let misunderstanding control your emotions
When others misunderstand you, do not rush to anger or retaliation, but learn to respond with humility and gentleness.
Lay down your burden and entrust by faith
You do not have to wait until the problem is solved to have peace. Believe that God hears prayer and be willing to give him the outcome.
q: What is the deepest sorrow and burden in my heart right now? Am I willing, like Hannah, to pour out my heart to God and, even before I see the result, entrust it by faith and let Jesus be King?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for being a God who hears prayer, full of love and mercy. You know the sorrow, grief, and troubles in my heart. Help me no longer carry them alone, but, like Hannah, pour out my heart to You. I am willing to lay down my anxiety and need to control, and let Jesus live in me and be King in me. Holy Spirit, comfort and guide my heart. Even when I have not yet seen the result, help me still believe in Your faithfulness, hand all my burdens to You, and live in peace and hope while waiting, so that all glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will pour out my heart before the LORD, entrust my burdens to him, and go forward by faith in peace!

t: Sanctified by Truth, One in Christ
v: Sanctify them in your truth. Your word is truth.
As you sent me into the world, even so I have sent them into the world.
For their sakes I sanctify myself, that they themselves also may be sanctified in truth.
“Not for these only do I pray, but for those also who will believe in me through their word,
that they may all be one; even as you, Father, are in me, and I in you, that they also may be one in us; that the world may believe that you sent me.
The glory which you have given me, I have given to them, that they may be one, even as we are one,
I in them, and you in me, that they may be perfected into one, that the world may know that you sent me and loved them, even as you loved me.
Father, I desire that they also whom you have given me be with me where I am, that they may see my glory which you have given me, for you loved me before the foundation of the world.
Righteous Father, the world hasn’t known you, but I knew you; and these knew that you sent me.
I made known to them your name, and will make it known; that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I in them.”
b: Just before going to the cross, Jesus prayed to the Father for his disciples: “Sanctify them in your truth. Your word is truth.” True holiness is not polishing behavior with outward rules, but letting God’s truth change life from within.

The old self centers on itself and lives by its own ideas, tastes, and desires; God’s truth helps us know his will, turn from sin, and live a life that belongs to God. Change your mindset and your life changes; change your life and your way of living changes. When we take the Bible as our Standard and the Holy Spirit as our Guide, lay down our own sovereignty, and let Jesus be King, we move from self to selflessness, and Christ’s holiness, humility, and love are lived out in us.

Jesus then prayed for all who believe in him: “that they may all be one.” This shows us that true unity is not everyone thinking the same, but everyone centered on Jesus and living in his truth and love. A self-centered life insists on its own opinion, position, and interests, easily producing comparison, rivalry, and division; a selfless life is willing to lay down pride and respect, accept, and complete one another.

The unity Jesus prayed for takes the oneness of the Father and the Son as its Role Model, so that believers love one another in Christ. When we no longer fight over who is lord, but together let Jesus be King, we can build relationships of unity, so that the world comes to know Christ from our love for one another.

Finally, Jesus made known his desire that his disciples be not only one on earth, but one day be with him and see his glory. He also asked that the Father’s love be in them and that he himself be in them. True victory is not only living out holiness and unity in this life, but being with Christ forever, in the hope of sharing his glory.

God’s redemption of us is not only to save individuals, but to make us a community in Christ that loves one another and is one in heart. Life first, then relationships, then ministry. When truth renews life, love builds relationships, and unity becomes the witness of the gospel, so that more people believe in Jesus and all glory goes to God.
a: Let truth sanctify your life
Do not only read and listen, but obey God’s word and let the Holy Spirit renew your mindset, so that you live out the life of Christ.
Lay yourself down and build unity
Do not insist on your own opinions, position, and interests, but accept and complete one another with humility and love.
Live out Christ and testify to God’s love
Let Jesus be King in your life, and build relationships with truth and love, so that more people come to know him through our unity.
q: Have I truly let God’s truth change my life? In my family, church, and spiritual companionships, do I insist on being king, or am I willing to lay down pride, let Jesus be King, and live out unity?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving me truth and life through Jesus Christ, and for calling me to live out holiness and unity. Sanctify me by Your truth and take away the pride, self-centeredness, and rivalry within me. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus live in me and be King in me. Holy Spirit, guide my life. Help me love my brothers and sisters in Christ and complete one another, build relationships of unity, and let the world know Jesus through our lives, and may I hope all my life to be with the Lord, giving all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will be sanctified by God’s truth, be one in Christ, live out his love, and let the world know Jesus!

t: Cry Out from the Depths and Wait for God’s Salvation
v: Out of the depths I have cried to you, LORD.
Lord, hear my voice.
If you, LORD, kept a record of sins,
But there is forgiveness with you,
I wait for the LORD.
My soul longs for the Lord more than watchmen long for the morning,
Israel, hope in the LORD,
He will redeem Israel from all their sins.
b: The psalmist cried to God from the depths of his life, confessing his iniquity and knowing that if God kept a record of sins, no one could stand. Yet he declared, “But there is forgiveness with you, therefore you are feared.” True hope is not that we have no sin, but that God has abundant grace of forgiveness.

The old self often covers up sin out of pride, or falls into self-blame because of failure; but God wants us to come before him humbly, truly confess our sin, and receive grace. True reverence is not leaving God out of fear, but, because we know his love and holiness, being willing to leave sin and let Jesus be King in life.

The psalmist went on, “I wait for the LORD. My soul waits. I hope in his word.” He compared waiting for God to a watchman waiting for the morning, expressing a firm and eager expectation. True faith is not demanding that God accomplish things at once as I want, but still believing his word while waiting.

When people meet difficulty, they often try to control the outcome with their own methods, and easily become anxious at delay. A selfless life is willing to lay down its own timetable, no longer letting its own will be king, and look to God alone. When we take the Bible as our Standard and the Holy Spirit as our Guide, we can still trust when we have not yet seen the answer, and still hope for the dawn in a long night.

Finally, the psalmist called on Israel to hope in the LORD, for with him is loving kindness and abundant redemption, and he will redeem his people from all their iniquities. God’s greatest salvation is not only delivering us from present trouble, but freeing us from sin’s dominion and restoring our relationship with him.

This abundant salvation is shown more fully in Jesus Christ. When we no longer rely on our own righteousness but trust in Christ’s redemption, we turn from guilt to forgiveness, from despair to hope, and from self to selflessness. Let Jesus live in us and be King in us, so that life is renewed by grace, we live out the life of Christ, and all glory goes to God.
a: Cry to God from the depths of your life
Do not hide your weakness and failure, but humbly confess your sin and receive God’s abundant forgiveness.
Hope in God’s word and wait patiently
Do not lose heart because prayer has not yet been answered. Lay down your timetable and firmly trust God’s promises.
Rely on salvation and live a new life
No longer be bound by guilt and failure. Let Jesus be King and by the Spirit live the life of one saved by grace.
q: When I am in difficulty, guilt, or a long wait, do I look for a way out by my own methods, or am I willing to humbly cry to God and hope in his word and abundant salvation?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for being full of love and forgiveness, and for being willing to hear my cry from the depths of my life. Forgive my sin, and take away the pride, self-centeredness, and unbelief within me, so that I no longer rely on my own righteousness and ability, but look to You alone. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus live in me and be King in me. Holy Spirit, guide my life. Help me trust Your word while waiting, hold on to hope in hardship, and live out the life of Christ in grace, giving all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will cry to the LORD from the depths, hope in his word, and wait for his abundant love and salvation!

t: Be Strong and Courageous, Move Toward the Promise by God’s Strength
v: Now after the death of Moses the servant of the LORD, the LORD spoke to Joshua the son of Nun, Moses’ servant, saying,
“Moses my servant is dead. Now therefore arise, go across this Jordan, you and all these people, to the land which I am giving to them, even to the children of Israel.
I have given you every place that the sole of your foot will tread on, as I told Moses.
From the wilderness and this Lebanon even to the great river, the river Euphrates, all the land of the Hittites, and to the great sea toward the going down of the sun, shall be your border.
No man will be able to stand before you all the days of your life. As I was with Moses, so I will be with you. I will not fail you nor forsake you.
“Be strong and courageous; for you shall cause this people to inherit the land which I swore to their fathers to give them.

Only be strong and very courageous. Be careful to observe to do according to all the law which Moses my servant commanded you. Don’t turn from it to the right hand or to the left, that you may have good success wherever you go.

This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written in it; for then you shall make your way prosperous, and then you shall have good success.
b: After Moses died, Joshua faced a major change in life. He had to take over the responsibility of leading the people and lead Israel across the Jordan into the Promised Land. God said to him, “Now therefore arise.” True faith is not waiting until all difficulties disappear before acting, but, because we believe God’s promise, courageously taking the step of obedience.

Joshua could not stay forever in Moses’ time, nor shrink back because the responsibility was great. God called him to arise and take on a new mission. When we lay down our fear and unease, no longer rely on past experience, and let Jesus be King, we can move forward courageously in new challenges.

God then promised Joshua, “As I was with Moses, so I will be with you. I will not fail you nor forsake you.” What truly makes a person strong and courageous is not his own ability, but God’s faithful presence. Though Joshua did not have Moses’ experience, he had the leading of the same God.

God’s work does not stop when people are replaced, because it is God who truly reigns. The old self easily fears for lack of faith, or becomes proud because of ability; a humble life is willing to admit its limits and rely on God alone. When we no longer let ourselves be king but let Jesus reign, we can experience God’s power in weakness.

Finally, God told Joshua to meditate on the book of the law day and night, to observe and do it, and not to turn from it to the right or the left. True prosperity is not everything succeeding as we wish, but walking in God’s will and completing the mission he has entrusted. God wanted Joshua not only to be courageous, but to obey the truth.

Courage without the guidance of truth easily becomes pride; faith without obedient action is only empty talk. When we take the Bible as our Standard and the Holy Spirit as our Guide and let Jesus be King, we turn from our own mindset to God’s mindset, from relying on ourselves to relying on Christ, and go forward faithfully in daily life and service, so that all glory goes to God.
a: Take the next step courageously by faith
When facing new challenges and charges, do not shrink back in fear, but trust God’s leading and act courageously.
Rely on God’s presence and be strong and courageous
Do not take your own ability and experience as your security, but believe in God’s faithfulness and humbly rely on him.
Meditate day and night, observe and do God’s word
Do not only read and listen, but put truth into practice in life and walk in the way that pleases God.
q: In what matter is God calling me now to arise and take a step of faith? Am I willing to lay down fear and self-centeredness, rely on God’s presence, and observe and do his word?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for being a faithful, covenant-keeping God who is with me always. When I face new challenges and missions, take away my fear and unease, so that I no longer rely on my own ability, but go forward courageously, strong and bold by faith. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus live in me and be King in me. Holy Spirit, guide my steps. Help me meditate on Your word every day, observe and do Your will without turning to the right or the left, and faithfully complete the mission You have entrusted to me, giving all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will be strong and courageous, meditate on and obey God’s word day and night, for he will not fail me nor forsake me!

t: A Sinner Shown Mercy, Made a Vessel God Can Use
v: I thank him who enabled me, Christ Jesus our Lord, because he counted me faithful, appointing me to service,
although I used to be a blasphemer, a persecutor, and insolent. However, I obtained mercy because I did it ignorantly in unbelief.
The grace of our Lord abounded exceedingly with faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.
The saying is faithful and worthy of all acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am chief.
However, for this cause I obtained mercy, that in me first, Jesus Christ might display all his patience for an example of those who were going to believe in him for eternal life.
Now to the King eternal, immortal, invisible, to God who alone is wise, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.
b: Paul looked back on his past life: he had blasphemed God, persecuted Christians, and even harmed many innocent people. Yet Christ Jesus not only showed him mercy, but gave him strength and called him to be an apostle of the gospel. What truly changes a life is not human effort and merit, but God’s abundant mercy and grace.

Paul was not proud of his achievements; the more he knew God’s grace, the more he saw his own unworthiness. Pride makes people exalt themselves; humility makes people exalt Christ. When we no longer prove our worth by our performance but humbly receive salvation, we can turn from self-centeredness to being Christ-centered.

Paul declared, “Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners.” This is the heart of the gospel. Jesus came into the world not to help good people become better, but to save sinners and give people a completely new life.

Paul called himself the foremost of sinners, yet because of Christ’s patience and mercy he became a testimony of one saved by grace. This shows us that however much we have failed in the past, if we truly repent and believe in Jesus, we can receive forgiveness and new life. The gospel is not patching up the old self’s life, but, through Christ’s redemption, moving us from self to selflessness, no longer letting ourselves be king, but letting Christ live within.

Finally, Paul gave all honor and glory to the King eternal, the only God. A person who has truly received grace does not turn God’s grace into his own glory, but lets his life become a testimony that shows God’s glory.

Paul went from persecuting the church to proclaiming the gospel not because he deserved it, but because God’s grace made him a vessel God could use. Today God likewise calls us not only to be saved by grace ourselves, but to live out Christ and serve others. When we take Jesus as our Role Model, the Bible as our Standard, and the Holy Spirit as our Guide, and let Jesus be King, we can faithfully fulfill what God entrusts to us, so that all glory goes to him.
a: Remember grace and keep a humble heart
Do not forget that you too are a sinner shown mercy. Do not be proud of gifts and achievements, but thank God for his mercy in everything.
Lay down the old self and live a new life
No longer be bound by past sins and failures. By faith receive Christ’s redemption and let Jesus be King in your life.
Serve faithfully and give God the glory
Do not treat service as your own merit, but rely on the strength the Lord gives and become a vessel that proclaims the gospel and blesses others.
q: Do I truly understand that I am a sinner shown mercy? Are the gifts, abilities, and service I have today used to exalt myself, or to let Jesus be King and show God’s abundant grace?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for saving me through Jesus Christ, and for showing abundant mercy and grace to an unworthy sinner like me. Take away my pride and self-centeredness, so that I no longer rely on my own ability or am bound by past failure. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus live in me and be King in me. Holy Spirit, guide my life. Give me faith, love, and faithfulness, so that I become a vessel You can use, live out the life of Christ, proclaim Your salvation, and give all honor and glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners! I have been shown mercy, and by the strength the Lord gives I will serve faithfully, so that all glory goes to God!

t: Hold Each Other Up and Go Farther Together
v: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor.
For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him who is alone when he falls, and doesn’t have another to lift him up.
Again, if two lie together, then they have warmth; but how can one keep warm alone?
If a man prevails against one who is alone, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
b: Ecclesiastes tells us, “Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor.” This shows us that God did not create people to live alone, but to hold one another up and complete one another in relationship.

A self-centered life puts itself at the center of everything, likes to control alone, and thinks it does not need others; a selfless life is willing to lay down pride and learn to work with others in one heart. True companionship is not only getting things done more efficiently, but making each other’s lives more mature. When we no longer fight over who is more important, but let Jesus be King, we can build relationships of unity in humility and love, so that our shared effort bears good fruit.

Ecclesiastes goes on, “If they fall, the one will lift up his fellow.” A true spiritual companion does not only celebrate together in success, but holds each other up in weakness, falling, and difficulty. Everyone has times of weariness, discouragement, and failure, so we need people who are willing to accompany, remind, encourage, and pray for us.

A spiritual companion does not only agree with us, but builds us up with love and truth. People matter more than tasks, and relationships matter more than things. When we are willing to lay down our own interests and face and stop caring only for ourselves, we can become people who support others and also humbly receive others’ help, so that each of us can stand again and keep going.

Finally, Ecclesiastes uses the picture of a cord of three strands to show the strength that comes from being joined together. A truly firm spiritual relationship is held not by human emotion, but by the truth and love of Christ as its foundation.

One person is easily weak, two can hold each other up, and more people united in heart can carry a mission together. This is an important principle for building spiritual companions, a spiritual family, and spiritual comrades. Life first, then relationships, then ministry. When we take Jesus as our Role Model, the Bible as our Standard, and the Holy Spirit as our Guide and lay down self-centeredness, we move from individual victory to team victory and together build God’s system, so that all glory goes to God.
a: Build spiritual companions who trust one another
Do not carry everything alone. Take the initiative to build relationships where you can share, pray, and hold one another up.
Hold one another up in weakness
When a companion falls, do not criticize and judge, but encourage and accompany him in love, helping him stand again.
Lay yourself down and complete the mission together
Do not fight over position and credit. Let Jesus be King, work together, complete one another, and serve God as one.
q: Do I have spiritual companions in my life whom I can trust and hold up, and who hold me up? Am I willing to lay down pride, not only receive help from others, but take the initiative to be someone who supports others?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for helping me understand that two are better than one, and for giving me spiritual companions who love one another and hold one another up. Take away the pride, self-centeredness, and desire to control alone within me, so that I am willing to humbly receive help and gladly support others. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus live in me and be King in me. Holy Spirit, guide my life. Help us build relationships of unity with truth and love, hold one another up in weakness, complete one another in service, live out the life of Christ together, and fulfill Your charge, giving all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Two are better than one! I will hold up my spiritual companions and be one with them in heart, and by the Lord bear good fruit!

t: Fear God and Welcome the Sun of Righteousness
v: “For behold, the day comes, burning like a furnace, when all the proud and all who work wickedness will be stubble. The day that comes will burn them up,” says the LORD of Armies, “so that it will leave them neither root nor branch.
But to you who fear my name shall the sun of righteousness arise with healing in its wings. You will go out and leap like calves of the stall.
You shall tread down the wicked; for they will be ashes under the soles of your feet in the day that I make,” says the LORD of Armies.
“Remember the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded to him in Horeb for all Israel, even statutes and ordinances.
Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the great and terrible day of the LORD comes.
He will turn the hearts of the fathers to the children and the hearts of the children to their fathers, lest I come and strike the earth with a curse.”
b: The prophet Malachi declared that the day of the LORD is coming, and the arrogant and all who do evil will face God’s righteous judgment. The real crisis is not how much wealth, power, and achievement a person has today, but whether his life truly fears God when his judgment comes.

Pride makes people leave their position, want to be king, and even think they can manage life without God; humility makes people admit their limits and be willing to return to God. God is loving, and he is also righteous; he will not tolerate sin forever. When we lay down self-centeredness, stop insisting on our own way, and let Jesus be King, we can turn from pride to humility, from rebellion to obedience, and prepare to welcome the day of the Lord.

God then promised those who fear his name, “The sun of righteousness will arise with healing in its rays.” This is a picture full of hope, showing that God’s righteousness and salvation will bring renewal and joy to those who fear him. The same day of God is judgment for those who persist in rebellion, but salvation and hope for those who fear him.

Christians also see in this promise the light of salvation that Jesus Christ brings. Through the cross and the resurrection, he enables sinners to be forgiven by faith and enter new life. True healing is not only outward difficulties being resolved, but the relationship between a person and God being restored. When we take the Bible as our Standard and the Holy Spirit as our Guide, we let Christ’s truth renew life and live out light and hope in the darkness.

Finally, God told the people to remember the law of Moses, and foretold that before the day of the LORD he would send Elijah, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children and the hearts of the children to their fathers. The New Testament shows that John the Baptist came in the spirit and power of Elijah to prepare the people to welcome Christ. True revival is not only an increase in outward religious activity, but hearts turning back to God and lives and relationships being renewed.

Self-centeredness makes people compete with, hurt, and divide from one another; selflessness makes people willing to repent humbly, forgive one another, and love again. Life first, then relationships, then ministry. When we let Jesus live and be King within, we can build united families and spiritual relationships, and prepare to welcome the Lord’s return with holiness and love.
a: Leave pride and fear God
Stop exalting yourself and doing as you please. Humbly examine your life each day and obey God’s will.
Look to Christ and live in the light of salvation
Do not be bound by sin, fear, and darkness. Trust Jesus’ salvation and by the Spirit live a new life.
Restore relationships and prepare to welcome the Lord
Take the initiative to forgive, care for, and complete your family and spiritual companions, building relationships of mutual love and unity.
q: If today were the day the Lord returns, is my life ready? Do I truly fear God and let Jesus be King, and am I willing to lay down pride and restore relationships that need reconciliation?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for being righteous, holy, and full of love. Shine Your light on me, so that I see the pride, self-centeredness, and disobedience within me, and am willing to truly repent and follow You with a heart of reverence. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus live in me and be King in me. Holy Spirit, renew my life. Help me live in the light of Christ’s salvation, learn to forgive and love one another, restore broken relationships, and live a life of holiness and unity, preparing to welcome the Lord Jesus’ return, giving all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will fear the LORD and welcome the sun of righteousness, be renewed in life, and be ready to meet the Lord!

t: Live Out Eternal Hope in Trials
v: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy caused us to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
to an incorruptible and undefiled inheritance that doesn’t fade away, reserved in Heaven for you,
who by the power of God are guarded through faith for a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.
In this you greatly rejoice, though now for a little while, if need be, you have been grieved in various trials,
that the proof of your faith, which is more precious than gold that perishes, even though it is tested by fire, may be found to result in praise, glory, and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ—
whom, not having known, you love. In him, though now you don’t see him, yet believing, you rejoice greatly with joy that is unspeakable and full of glory,
receiving the result of your faith, the salvation of your souls.
b: Peter reminded believers that God, through Jesus Christ’s resurrection from the dead, has given us new birth into a living hope, and an inheritance kept in heaven that cannot perish or fade. True hope is not expecting this life to be always smooth, but that, because Jesus has risen, we have eternal life and an eternal inheritance.

People often build their security on wealth, health, and achievement, forgetting that all of it changes. When we turn from the earthly viewpoint to the heavenly one, from the temporary to the eternal, we are no longer controlled by the gains and losses of circumstances, but let Jesus be King and live out a firm hope in his salvation.

Peter went on to point out that although believers may be briefly grieved by various trials, they can still greatly rejoice, because faith that has been tested is more precious than gold refined by fire. True faith is not never meeting difficulty, but still relying on God in difficulty, so that life becomes more mature.

Trials reveal what our lives truly rely on: our own ability, or God’s grace. A self-centered life easily complains and loses heart in difficulty; a selfless life is willing to lay itself down, be guided by the Spirit, and learn trust and obedience in hardship. God can use trials to refine our faith so that the life of Christ shines out more.
Finally, Peter said, “Whom, not having seen, you love.” This shows us that true joy comes not from the circumstances our eyes see, but from a real life relationship with Jesus Christ.

Though we have not seen Jesus with our own eyes, we can love him because we believe in him, and in him we have joy that is full of glory and cannot be expressed in words. When we no longer fix our focus on ourselves, others, and circumstances, but look to Jesus alone, we can still be full of hope in trials. Take Jesus as our Role Model, the Bible as our Standard, and the Holy Spirit as our Guide, and let Christ live in us and be King in us until the day we see his face, so that all glory goes to God.
a: Look to the risen Lord and hold on to eternal hope
Do not measure life by earthly wealth and achievement, but treasure the heavenly inheritance God has prepared that cannot perish or fade.
Stand firm in faith in trials
Do not lose heart because of difficulty. Learn to rely on God’s power and let trials become an opportunity for faith to grow.
Love Jesus and live out heavenly joy
Do not let circumstances decide your joy. Draw near to Jesus every day, let the Holy Spirit guide your life, and live out the life of Christ.
q: When I face trials and difficulties, am I controlled by present sorrow, or do I hold on to eternal hope because of the salvation of Jesus’ resurrection, letting faith become firmer in trials?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for raising Jesus Christ from the dead, so that I am born again to a living hope and an eternal inheritance. When I face trials and difficulties, keep my faith, so that I am not controlled by circumstances and sorrow, but look to Jesus alone. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus live in me and be King in me. Holy Spirit, guide my life. Refine my faith through trials, so that I love You and trust You more, live out the life of Christ, and am full of heavenly joy and hope, giving all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Through the resurrection of Jesus Christ I have a living hope; in trials my faith is more precious, and in believing in the Lord I greatly rejoice!

t: From Brokenness to Restoration, Living Out God’s Glory
v: The Lord GOD’s Spirit is on me,
to proclaim the year of the LORD’s favor
to provide for those who mourn in Zion,
They will rebuild the old ruins.
Strangers will stand and feed your flocks.
But you will be called the LORD’s priests.
Instead of your shame you will have double.
b: Isaiah declared that the Spirit of the Lord GOD anoints his sent servant to bring good news, to heal the brokenhearted, and to proclaim release to the captives. Jesus quoted this passage in the synagogue at Nazareth and declared that the prophecy was fulfilled in him. The gospel is not only telling people how they should live, but Jesus coming himself to save people, so that lives bound by sin receive freedom.

The greatest problem of humanity is that the old self centers on itself and wants to be king, and as a result is ruled by sin. Through the cross and the resurrection, Jesus accomplished salvation, so that we can be freed from the power of sin and receive new life. When we humbly believe in him and let Jesus be King, we move from self to selflessness and experience true freedom.

God promised to give a garland instead of ashes, the oil of joy instead of mourning, and the garment of praise instead of a spirit of heaviness, so that those who receive grace become oaks of righteousness, the planting of the LORD. True restoration of life is not only a change in outward circumstances, but God making a broken life take root again, living out righteousness and joy.

People may lose hope because of past failures, hurts, and shame, but God’s grace can make a person stand again. This is not a guarantee that every difficulty will vanish at once, but that God can give comfort and renewal in pain. When we are no longer bound by the past, but take the Bible as our Standard and the Holy Spirit as our Guide, we can let Christ’s life grow within us, turn from sorrow to hope, and bear fruit that glorifies God.

Finally, God promised that his people would rebuild the ancient ruins, raise up the former devastations, and be those who serve him. God restores our lives not only so that we ourselves are blessed, but to use us to repair broken relationships and rebuild desolate lives.

A self-centered life cares only about its own needs; a selfless life is willing to be a channel of God’s grace, caring for, supporting, and completing others. Life first, then relationships, then ministry. When we first experience the renewal of the gospel, we can build relationships of mutual love and bear God’s mission together. Let Jesus live in us and be King in us, so that desolation becomes abundance and all glory goes to God.
a: Receive the gospel and live out true freedom
No longer let sin, pride, and self-centeredness rule your life. Let Jesus be King and by the Spirit live a new life.
Lay down the past and experience renewal of life
Do not be bound by failure, shame, and pain. Look to God’s grace and let him restore the hope and joy in your life.
Be a blessing and rebuild broken lives
Do not only receive grace yourself, but care for the brokenhearted, walk with the weak, and become a vessel for God’s restoration of lives.
q: In what areas of my life am I bound by sin, pain, or past failures, needing Jesus to set me free and renew me? Am I willing to be God’s vessel to help others move from brokenness to restoration?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for bringing the gospel through Jesus Christ, so that those bound by sin are set free and the brokenhearted are comforted. Heal the brokenness in my life, and take away my pride, self-centeredness, and the bonds of the past, so that I receive hope and joy again. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus live in me and be King in me. Holy Spirit, renew and guide my life. Make me an oak of righteousness that You have planted, live out the life of Christ, and be a vessel that comforts people, holds them up, and rebuilds lives, so that all glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will be set free and healed by the Lord, take joy instead of mourning, become an oak of righteousness planted by God, and bring him glory!

t: Lay Yourself Down and Live Out the Mind of Christ
v: If therefore there is any exhortation in Christ, if any consolation of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit, if any tender mercies and compassion,
make my joy full by being like-minded, having the same love, being of one accord, of one mind;
doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself;
each of you not just looking to his own things, but each of you also to the things of others.
Have this in your mind, which was also in Christ Jesus,
b: Paul urged the church in Philippi to be of the same mind and the same love, one in heart, in the love of Christ and the fellowship of the Spirit. True unity is not everyone doing things my way, but everyone being willing to lay themselves down and let Jesus be King.

The old self easily insists on its own opinion and seeks approval, and even creates distance because of differing opinions; but Christ’s love makes us learn to accept, understand, and complete one another. Unity is not removing all differences, but sharing a common direction in truth and love. When we no longer center on ourselves but on Jesus, we can move from rivalry to unity and build spiritual relationships of mutual love.

Paul went on, “Doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself.” Pride makes people compete for rank; humility makes people complete one another. Self brings division; selflessness brings unity.

Pride is leaving man’s position and grasping power, exalting oneself; humility is laying down our own sovereignty, returning to our position, and letting God be God. To count others better than ourselves is not to deny our own worth, but to be willing to respect and appreciate others, no longer putting our own interests first. When we lay down pride, no longer fighting for position, face, and credit, humility overcomes pride, and the love of Christ is shown in our relationships.

Finally, Paul pointed out, “Each of you not just looking to his own things, but each of you also to the things of others.” And he urged us, “Have this in your mind, which was also in Christ Jesus.” True denying of self is not neglecting ourselves, but no longer caring only for ourselves, and being willing to live for Jesus and for others.

Jesus is our most perfect Role Model of humility, self-denial, and service. When we take Jesus as our Role Model, the Bible as our Standard, and the Holy Spirit as our Guide, we move from the life of self to the life of selflessness. Life first, then relationships, then ministry: only when Christ first changes our hearts can we build relationships of unity, together complete God’s mission, and give all glory to him.
a: Lay yourself down and pursue unity
Do not insist on your own opinions and interests. Accept and complete one another in the love of Christ.
Keep a humble mind and value others
Do not fight over position, face, and credit. Learn to respect and appreciate others, letting man be man and God be God.
Take the mind of Christ as your mind
Do not look only to your own things, but also to the things of others, and live out Jesus’ humble, self-denying life in daily life and service.
q: In my family, church, and spiritual companionships, am I still insisting on my own way and seeking my own glory? In what matter am I willing to lay myself down and have the mind of Christ Jesus?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for letting me know true humility and love through Jesus Christ. Shine Your light on me, so that I see the pride, self-centeredness, and desire for empty glory within me. I am willing to lay myself down, no longer caring only for my own things, but learning to respect, understand, and complete others. Holy Spirit, guide me, let Jesus live in me and be King in me, so that I have the mind of Christ, build relationships of mutual love and unity, live out a humble, self-denying life, and give all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will have the mind of Christ Jesus, keep a humble mind, look not only to my own things but also to those of others, and live out unity!

t: Affliction Turned Me Back, Truth Benefited Me
v: You have treated your servant well,
Teach me good judgment and knowledge,
Before I was afflicted, I went astray;
You are good, and do good.
The proud have smeared a lie upon me.
Their heart is as callous as the fat,
It is good for me that I have been afflicted,
The law of your mouth is better to me than thousands of pieces of gold and silver.
b: The psalmist looked back on his life and honestly admitted, “Before I was afflicted, I went astray, but now I observe your word.” This shows us that affliction is not necessarily life’s failure; it can also be an opportunity for a life to turn back and know God again.

When life goes smoothly, people easily rely on their own cleverness and ability and, without noticing, stray from God’s way; but when difficulty comes, they find their own limits. Affliction does not automatically change a person; the key is whether we are willing to be humbly taught. When we lay down pride, stop insisting on our own will, and let God’s truth correct our mindset, we can turn from going astray to obedience and let Jesus be King in life again.

The psalmist then declared, “You are good, and do good.” Even when attacked by the lies of the proud, he still chose to keep God’s precepts with his whole heart. True faith is not believing God is good only when circumstances go well, but being sure in affliction that God’s nature and word never change.

A self-centered life is easily moved by others’ criticism, attacks, and circumstances, quick to defend and strike back; a selfless life is willing to lay itself down and turn its focus back to God. When we take the Bible as our Standard and the Holy Spirit as our Guide, we do not let others’ evil decide our reactions, but hold to truth and live out Christ’s humility and goodness.

Finally, the psalmist said, “It is good for me that I have been afflicted, that I may learn your statutes,” and declared that the law from God’s mouth is better than thousands of pieces of gold and silver. The true wealth of life is not how much gold and silver we have, but how much of God’s truth we understand and obey.

People often hope God will remove difficulties quickly, but God can use difficulties to help us see our problems and make our lives more mature. This does not mean that all suffering is God’s discipline, but that we can learn to trust him in suffering. Change your mindset and your life changes; change your life and your way of living changes. When we turn from pursuing earthly wealth to treasuring eternal truth, we can live a life more like Christ, so that all glory goes to God.
a: Be humbly taught in affliction
Do not only ask God to remove difficulty, but examine yourself and learn the lesson God teaches through truth.
Hold to truth even when attacked
Do not lose peace because of others’ criticism and misunderstanding. Let God’s word guide your thoughts and actions.
Treasure truth above earthly wealth
Do not only pursue money, achievement, and pleasure, but learn and obey God’s word every day and live out the life of Christ.
q: Is the difficulty I face now reminding me that I need to change some mindsets or ways of living? Am I willing to humbly receive God’s teaching and let his truth be the most precious wealth of my life?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that You are good and do good, and that You always deal well with me according to Your word. When I face affliction, attack, and difficulty, keep me from complaining and losing heart, and help me humbly seek Your will. I am willing to lay down pride and self-centeredness and let Jesus live in me and be King in me. Holy Spirit, guide my life. Renew my mindset by truth, so that I turn from going astray to obedience, treasure Your word above the gold and silver of the earth, and live out the life of Christ, giving all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: It is good for me that I have been afflicted, that I may learn God’s statutes; I will treasure his word more than thousands of pieces of gold and silver!

t: The Savior Is Born, Glory to God
v: While they were there, the day had come for her to give birth.
She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.
There were shepherds in the same country staying in the field, and keeping watch by night over their flock.
Behold, an angel of the Lord stood by them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they were terrified.
The angel said to them, “Don’t be afraid, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy which will be to all the people.
For there is born to you today, in David’s city, a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.
This is the sign to you: you will find a baby wrapped in strips of cloth, lying in a feeding trough.”
Suddenly, there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly army praising God and saying,
“Glory to God in the highest,
When the angels went away from them into the sky, the shepherds said to one another, “Let’s go to Bethlehem, now, and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.”
They came with haste and found both Mary and Joseph, and the baby was lying in the feeding trough.
b: Jesus Christ is the King of kings, yet he was not born in a magnificent palace, but in humble surroundings, laid in a manger. The Son of God humbled himself and came into the world not to seek human honor, but to save sinners and show God’s love.

The old self loves to pursue position, power, and glory, but Jesus became our Role Model with a humble life. Though he was in the form of God, he willingly humbled himself and entered human suffering. True greatness is not exalting ourselves, but being willing to give ourselves up for love. When we lay down pride, no longer center on ourselves, and let Jesus be King, we can live out the humble, self-giving life of Christ.

The angel declared to the shepherds, “Don’t be afraid, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy which will be to all the people.” The greatest good news of the gospel is not that people’s circumstances become better, but that the Savior, Jesus Christ, has been born, so that sinners can be reconciled to God.

God did not first send this news to powerful kings, but let shepherds working in the fields hear it first. This shows that God’s salvation is not the privilege of a few, but good news to be spread to all people. The angels declared glory to God and peace among those with whom he is pleased. True peace is not only no war outside, but restoring our relationship with God through Jesus Christ, so that life has eternal hope.

Finally, when the shepherds heard the angel’s message, they said to one another, “Let’s go to Bethlehem and see this thing that has happened.” They did not stay in wonder and emotion, but took immediate action to find the Savior who was born. True faith is not only hearing the gospel, but being willing to respond to it and come to Jesus ourselves.

Today we cannot treat Jesus’ birth only as a holiday or a historical story. We must let him truly enter our lives and become our Savior and the King of our lives. When we take Jesus as our Role Model, the Bible as our Standard, and the Holy Spirit as our Guide, we move from knowing Jesus to living out Jesus, and pass the good news of salvation to more people, so that all glory goes to God.
a: Imitate Jesus and live out humility
Do not pursue your own position and glory. Be willing to lay down pride and serve others in the love of Christ.
Receive the Savior and gain true peace
Do not only know the story of Jesus’ birth, but believe in his salvation and let Jesus be King in your life.
Respond to the gospel and proclaim the good news
Do not only receive salvation yourself, but take the initiative to share Jesus with others, so that more people know the Savior.
q: Jesus has been born as the Savior of all people. Do I truly let him be King in my life, or do I only stay at knowing his story without living out his humble, self-giving life?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving Jesus Christ in love, so that the Savior was born and brought us salvation and peace. Take away the pride, self-centeredness, and pursuit of empty glory within me, so that I imitate Jesus’ humility and self-denial. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus live in me and be King in me. Holy Spirit, guide my life. Help me not only receive the good news of the gospel, but live out the love of Christ and pass salvation to more people, so that all glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: The Savior, Christ, has been born! I will joyfully receive his salvation, let Jesus be King, and give glory to God in the highest!

t: Seek Jesus and Let the True King Reign
v: Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of King Herod, behold, wise men from the east came to Jerusalem, saying,
“Where is he who is born King of the Jews? For we saw his star in the east, and have come to worship him.”
When King Herod heard it, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
Gathering together all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he asked them where the Christ would be born.
They said to him, “In Bethlehem of Judea, for this is written through the prophet,
‘You Bethlehem, land of Judah,
He sent them to Bethlehem, and said, “Go and search diligently for the young child. When you have found him, bring me word, so that I also may come and worship him.”
They, having heard the king, went their way; and behold, the star, which they saw in the east, went before them until it came and stood over where the young child was.
When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy.
They came into the house and saw the young child with Mary, his mother, and they fell down and worshiped him. Opening their treasures, they offered to him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
Being warned in a dream not to return to Herod, they went back to their own country another way.
b: When Jesus was born, the wise men from the east came from afar to seek the Christ who had been born King of the Jews. King Herod heard the news and was troubled, because he saw Jesus as a threat to his own throne. The same Jesus: some joyfully seek him, others fear losing power; the key is who will be king.

Herod represents the self-centered life, wanting to grasp power and protect his position; the wise men were willing to lay down their status and humbly seek the true King. Pride makes people resist Jesus; humility makes people draw near to Jesus. Today we also need to examine whether we still insist on being lord ourselves, or are willing to return to man’s position and let Jesus be King in life.

The chief priests and scribes knew the Scriptures and knew that the Christ would be born in Bethlehem, yet the wise men from the east, without sparing the hardship, kept seeking until they met Jesus. To truly know the Bible is not only to know the content of truth, but to be willing to obey it and come to Jesus ourselves.

Knowledge without faith and action cannot truly change a life. When the wise men saw the star, they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy, because the goal they sought was about to be reached. Today when we read the Bible, pray, and gather, we also must not stay in religious knowledge and activity, but let God’s word renew our mindset, so that we move from knowing Jesus to following Jesus, and from knowing truth to living out the life of Christ.

Finally, the wise men entered the house, saw Jesus, and fell down and worshiped him, offering gold, frankincense, and myrrh, and obeyed God’s direction and returned by another way. True worship is not only honoring Jesus with our mouths, but giving him what is most precious and letting him guide the way of our lives.

The wise men did not come to ask Jesus to fulfill their wishes, but to worship the true King, and their worship led to obedient action. When we take Jesus as our Role Model, the Bible as our Standard, and the Holy Spirit as our Guide, we can lay down our own sovereignty and give our lives, time, gifts, and everything to God. Let Jesus be King, let Jesus receive all the glory, and walk in the way that pleases God.
a: Lay down pride and let Jesus be King
Do not grasp your power like Herod, but humbly acknowledge that Jesus is the true King of your life.
Seek truth and follow Jesus yourself
Do not stay only at Bible knowledge, but actually obey God’s word, so that truth changes your life and your way of living.
Give yourself and respond to worship with obedience
Give the Lord your most precious time, gifts, and life, obey the guidance of the Holy Spirit, and walk in God’s way.
q: Facing Jesus, the true King, is my life more like Herod, who fears losing power, or like the wise men, who humbly seek and fall down to worship? What am I willing to lay down so that Jesus truly reigns?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for sending Jesus Christ to be born as our Savior and eternal King. Shine Your light on me, so that I see the pride, self-centeredness, and life that wants to be king within me. I am willing to follow the wise men, humbly seek Jesus, fall down and worship him, and give You everything most precious in my life. Holy Spirit, guide me, so that I not only understand the truth of the Bible but obey Your word, and let Jesus live in me and be King in me. May my life, my way of living, my relationships, and my service all honor the Lord, giving all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Like the wise men, I will humbly seek Jesus, worship the true King, give myself, let Jesus be King, and give all glory to God!

t: Fan the Gift into Flame, Live Out the Gospel with Strength
v: I thank God, whom I serve as my forefathers did, with a pure conscience. How unceasing is my memory of you in my petitions, night and day
longing to see you, remembering your tears, that I may be filled with joy;
having been reminded of the sincere faith that is in you, which lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice and, I am persuaded, in you also.
For this cause, I remind you that you should stir up the gift of God which is in you through the laying on of my hands.
For God didn’t give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
Therefore don’t be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner; but endure hardship for the Good News according to the power of God,
who saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given to us in Christ Jesus before times eternal,
but has now been revealed by the appearing of our Savior, Christ Jesus, who abolished death, and brought life and immortality to light through the Good News.
Hold the pattern of sound words which you have heard from me, in faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.
That good thing which was committed to you, guard through the Holy Spirit who dwells in us.
b: Writing to Timothy from prison, Paul did not think only of his own suffering, but prayed without ceasing for his spiritual son, remembering his sincere faith and reminding him to stir up again the gift God had given him. True spiritual inheritance is not only passing knowledge to the next generation, but living out real faith and love before them.

Timothy’s faith had a beautiful example in his grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice. Today we also need to build spiritual relationships of mutual care, prayer, and encouragement. Life first, then relationships, then ministry. When life is set on fire by God’s love, gifts can become vessels that bless others, so that the flame of the gospel is passed on without end.

Paul went on, “For God didn’t give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.” True strength is not our own courage and ability, but relying on the power God gives and following Jesus faithfully with love and self-control.

Paul did not promise Timothy that serving the Lord would bring no difficulty, but urged him not to be ashamed of the gospel and to share in suffering by God’s power. The old self easily shrinks back from fear of failure and concern for others’ opinions; a selfless life is willing to lay itself down and fix its focus on Jesus. Strength keeps us from shrinking back, love keeps us from hurting others, and self-control keeps us from acting as we please; only the three together can live out a mature life of Christ.

Finally, Paul reminded Timothy that salvation is not by our works but by God’s own purpose and grace, and that Christ has brought life and immortality to light through the gospel. He also charged Timothy to hold the pattern of sound words and, by the Holy Spirit who lives in us, to guard the good deposit entrusted to him.

True victory is not only serving with zeal, but holding to the truth of the gospel and being faithful to the end by the Spirit. Zeal apart from truth easily loses its direction; knowledge without love cannot build up life. When we take Jesus as our Role Model, the Bible as our Standard, and the Holy Spirit as our Guide, and let Jesus be King within, we can hold the faith, live out the gospel, and faithfully complete what God has entrusted, so that all glory goes to him.
a: Fan the gift into flame and pass on real faith
Do not let the gift God gave you grow cold. Take the initiative to care, pray, and serve, and be a spiritual example for the next generation.
Be strong and loving, and witness boldly to Christ
Do not shrink back from difficulty or others’ opinions. Rely on God’s power and live out the gospel with love and self-control.
Hold the true faith and serve by the Spirit
Do not only pursue zeal and power, but obey the truth of the Bible and guard the gospel you have received by the Spirit.
q: What gifts and charges has God given me? Have my gifts grown cold because of timidity, laziness, or self-centeredness? How will I rely on the Spirit today to stir up my gift again and serve the Lord with strength, love, and self-control?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for saving me through Jesus Christ, not because of my works, but out of Your abundant grace. Stir up again the faith and gifts within me, take away timidity, pride, and self-centeredness, and give me a spirit of power, love, and self-control. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus live in me and be King in me. Holy Spirit, guide me, so that I am not ashamed of the gospel, witness boldly for the Lord, am faithful in difficulty and serve in love, hold on to the sound faith, and become a vessel that passes on faith and builds up others, giving all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: God has not given me a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control! By the Spirit I will fan the gift into flame, hold the true faith, and faithfully witness to the gospel!

t: Let Christ Dwell in Your Heart and Live Out Boundless Love
v: that he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, that you may be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inner person,
that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith, to the end that you, being rooted and grounded in love,
may be strengthened to comprehend with all the saints what is the width and length and height and depth,
and to know Christ’s love which surpasses knowledge, that you may be filled with all the fullness of God.
b: Paul prayed for the church in Ephesus, asking that God, through his Spirit, strengthen believers with power in the inner being. True strength is not how great our outward ability is, but that within us is the life of Christ’s presence and the reign of the Holy Spirit.

People often build strength on knowledge, experience, wealth, and position, overlooking that the true strength of life comes from God. However strong we are outwardly, if inside we are full of fear, pride, and self-centeredness, we are still easily weak. God wants to change us not only by adding ability, but by renewing the inner life. When we lay ourselves down, no longer rule ourselves, but let the Spirit guide and Jesus be King, we move from self to selflessness, and the strength in our hearts grows firmer and firmer.

Paul then asked that Christ may dwell in our hearts through faith, so that our love is rooted and grounded. The true Christian life is not only believing that Jesus can help me, but letting Jesus live in me and be the Lord of my life. Like a tree, the deeper its roots, the better it withstands wind and rain; the deeper our lives are rooted in Christ’s love, the more firmly we can stand in difficulty.

A self-centered life centers on itself and easily calculates, compares, and competes; a selfless life lets Christ live within, giving us the power to be humble, forgive, accept, and complete others. Life first, then relationships, then ministry: only when life is first filled with Christ’s love can we build relationships of true mutual love.

Finally, Paul hoped that believers, together with all the saints, would be able to comprehend the breadth, length, height, and depth of Christ’s love and be filled with all the fullness of God. Christ’s love surpasses human measure; the more we know his love, the more we can lay down our limited selves and live out his abundant life.

We cannot fully fathom God’s love with our heads alone, but we can keep experiencing this love through faith, the work of the Holy Spirit, and a life of loving one another with all the saints. Selflessness is not losing the value of life, but no longer letting our limited self be king and letting the limitless Christ be shown in us. When we take Jesus as our Role Model, the Bible as our Standard, and the Holy Spirit as our Guide, we can live out the love of Christ, so that all glory goes to God.
a: Rely on the Spirit and strengthen your inner life
Do not only pursue outward ability and achievement, but draw near to God every day and let the Spirit renew your mind so that your life is strong.
Let Christ be King and your love rooted and grounded
No longer center on yourself. Let Jesus reign in your heart and build relationships with humility, forgiveness, and love.
Experience Christ’s love and live out an abundant life
With spiritual companions, hold each other up and complete one another, know Christ more deeply in love, and become a vessel that blesses others.
q: Who truly reigns in my heart: myself, or Jesus Christ? Am I willing to lay down pride and self-centeredness, let the Spirit strengthen my life, and let Christ’s love take root in me and flow out through my life?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for caring for me with abundant glory and boundless love. By Your Spirit, strengthen the power in my heart, and take away my pride, fear, and self-centeredness. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus dwell in my heart, live in me, and be King in me. Make my love rooted and grounded in Christ, so that together with all the saints I know more deeply the breadth, length, height, and depth of Christ’s love, and my life is filled more and more with Your fullness, living out humility, forgiveness, and mutual love, giving all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: By the Spirit I will be strengthened in my heart, let Christ dwell in my heart, be rooted and grounded in love, and be filled with his love in its breadth, length, height, and depth!

t: Immanuel, God with Us
v: Now the birth of Jesus Christ was like this: After his mother, Mary, was engaged to Joseph, before they came together, she was found pregnant by the Holy Spirit.
Joseph, her husband, being a righteous man, and not willing to make her a public example, intended to put her away secretly.

But when he thought about these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, “Joseph, son of David, don’t be afraid to take to yourself Mary as your wife, for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit.
She shall give birth to a son. You shall name him Jesus, for it is he who shall save his people from their sins.”
Now all this has happened that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying,
“Behold, the virgin shall be with child,
Joseph arose from his sleep, and did as the angel of the Lord commanded him, and took his wife to himself;
and didn’t know her sexually until she had given birth to her firstborn son. He named him Jesus.
b: When Joseph discovered that Mary, to whom he was engaged, was pregnant, he faced a situation hard to understand, and his heart must have been full of struggle. Yet he did not publicly shame Mary in anger, but planned to divorce her quietly. True righteousness is not only holding to what we think is right, but keeping mercy and love within the truth.

Joseph’s attitude shows us that when facing others’ problems, we should not rush to judge or hurt them. A self-centered life easily cares only about its own face, rights, and feelings; a humble life is willing to value others. People matter more than tasks, and relationships matter more than things. When we lay down self-centeredness and learn to have the mind of Jesus, we can live out gentleness and mercy even in difficult relationships.

While Joseph was considering how to deal with this, God made the truth known to him through an angel and told him not to be afraid to take Mary as his wife. When Joseph woke up, he did as God commanded. True faith is not obeying only after everything is understood, but, once God’s will is understood, being willing to lay down our own plans and obey courageously.

Joseph already had his own plan, but when God’s word came, he changed his decision. Humility is returning to man’s position, letting God be God, and no longer insisting on being king ourselves. Today we also need to take the Bible as our Standard and the Holy Spirit as our Guide, and let God’s truth correct our mindset, so that faith does not stay in the heart but is carried out in real action.

The angel declared that the son Mary would bear should be named Jesus, for he would save his people from their sins; he is also called Immanuel, “God with us.” The greatest grace of Jesus’ birth is not only that God came to the human world, but that God came himself to save sinners, so that we can be restored to relationship with him.

The greatest problem of humanity is not bad circumstances, but that sin makes people leave God and want to be lord and king themselves. Through the cross and the resurrection, Jesus accomplished salvation, so that we can be freed from the dominion of sin and receive new life. When we believe in Jesus and let him live in our hearts and be King in our lives, we move from self to selflessness, experience the grace of Immanuel every day, live out the life of Christ, and give glory to God.
a: Treat people with mercy and do not rush to judge
When facing others’ problems and misunderstandings, learn Joseph’s gentleness and do not hurt others to protect your own face.
Lay down your own will and obey God courageously
When God’s word corrects your thinking, be willing to lay down your original plan and obey his will by faith.
Let Jesus be King and experience God’s presence
Do not only celebrate Jesus’ birth, but receive his salvation and let him reign in your daily life.
q: When God’s will differs from my thinking, am I willing, like Joseph, to lay down my plans and obey by faith? Do I truly let Jesus save me from self-centeredness, living every day in the grace of God’s presence?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for sending Jesus Christ to be born as Immanuel, so that through his salvation I can be restored to relationship with You. Take away the pride, self-centeredness, and fear within me, so that like Joseph I treat people with a merciful heart and courageously obey Your will. I am willing to lay down my own plans and let Jesus live in me and be King in me. Holy Spirit, guide my life. Help me experience Your presence every day, be freed from the dominion of sin, live out the humble, obedient, loving life of Christ, and be a blessing to others, giving all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Jesus is my Savior, and Immanuel is my hope! I will lay myself down, obey God’s will, let Jesus be King, and live every day in God’s presence!

t: Hear the Gospel, Experience Jesus, Proclaim Salvation
v: When the angels went away from them into the sky, the shepherds said to one another, “Let’s go to Bethlehem, now, and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.”
