They came with haste and found both Mary and Joseph, and the baby was lying in the feeding trough.
When they saw it, they publicized widely the saying which was spoken to them about this child.
All who heard it wondered at the things which were spoken to them by the shepherds.
But Mary kept all these sayings, pondering them in her heart.
The shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things that they had heard and seen, just as it was told them.
b: When the shepherds heard the angel’s good news that the Savior was born, they did not stay in wonder and emotion, but at once said to one another, “Let’s go to Bethlehem.” They went with haste and found the baby Jesus lying in the manger. True faith is not only hearing God’s word, but believing it and taking obedient action.

Many people are deeply moved when they hear a message, yet return to life unchanged; the shepherds turned what they had heard into action. Change your mindset and your life changes; change your life and your way of living changes. When we no longer act only by our own thinking but take the Bible as our Standard and the Holy Spirit as our Guide, we move from hearing truth to obeying truth and experience the faithfulness of God’s word ourselves.

After the shepherds saw Jesus, they spread widely the word that had been told them about this child, while Mary kept all these things, pondering them in her heart. A true experience of the gospel needs not only bold proclaiming, but also thoughtful pondering, so that truth takes deep root in life.

The shepherds shared in words what they had heard and seen, and Mary quietly pondered God’s wonderful works; both are precious responses of faith. Today we also need to avoid having only outward zeal while lacking inward renewal of life. First let God’s word enter our hearts and change our mindset and life, and then witness to Christ with real living. Life first, then relationships, then ministry. When Jesus is King within us, the gospel we proclaim can be shown more fully through our lives.

Finally, the shepherds returned to their former life and work, yet because of all they had heard and seen, they glorified and praised God. Those who truly meet Jesus do not necessarily change their work and circumstances at once, but they can return to their old life with a renewed life and live differently.

The shepherds were still shepherds, but their hearts were filled with the joy of the Savior’s birth. Today we also need not wait for our circumstances to change completely before we live out the life of Christ. When we lay down self-centeredness, no longer live for ourselves, but let Jesus live and be King within, we can proclaim the gospel in our families, workplaces, and service, give thanks in everything, and give all glory to God.
a: Hear the truth and obey at once
Do not let Bible reading and listening stay at emotion. Take the initiative to put God’s word into practice every day.
Ponder thoughtfully and live out the gospel
Learn from Mary to keep God’s word in your heart and ponder it, letting truth renew your mindset and life.
Share your testimony and give God the glory
Like the shepherds, introduce the Savior you know to others, and praise and glorify God in daily life.
q: After I hear God’s word, do I stay at knowing and being moved, or am I willing to obey at once? Do I keep Jesus’ salvation in my heart and ponder it, live out Christ in daily life, and let people know him through my testimony?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for sending Jesus Christ to be born and bringing us the good news of salvation. Help me, like the shepherds, to respond by faith and obey boldly when I hear Your word, and, like Mary, to keep Your word in my heart and ponder it. I am willing to lay down my pride and self-centeredness and let Jesus live in me and be King in me. Holy Spirit, guide my life. Give me not only outward zeal but inward renewal, so that in my family, workplace, and service I live out the love of Christ, proclaim the gospel boldly, give thanks and praise in everything, and give all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Like the shepherds, I will believe when I hear, act when I believe, proclaim when I experience, praise God in everything, and give all glory to him!

t: Understand God’s Word and Receive the Strength of Joy
v: Ezra the priest brought the law before the assembly, both men and women, and all who could hear with understanding, on the first day of the seventh month.

He read from it before the wide place that was in front of the water gate from early morning until midday, in the presence of the men and the women, and of those who could understand. The ears of all the people were attentive to the book of the law.

Ezra the scribe stood on a pulpit of wood, which they had made for the purpose; and beside him stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah, on his right hand; and on his left hand, Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
Then Ezra blessed the LORD, the great God.
They read in the book, in the law of God, distinctly; and they gave the sense, so that they understood the reading.

Nehemiah, who was the governor, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who taught the people said to all the people, “Today is holy to the LORD your God. Don’t mourn, nor weep.” For all the people wept when they heard the words of the law.

Then he said to them, “Go your way. Eat the fat, drink the sweet, and send portions to him for whom nothing is prepared, for today is holy to our Lord. Don’t be grieved, for the joy of the LORD is your strength.”
b: After returning from exile and rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem, the people of Israel gathered in front of the Water Gate to listen to God’s law. From early morning until midday, all listened attentively, while Ezra and the Levites read clearly and gave the sense, so that the people truly understood. True spiritual revival is not only rebuilding outward buildings and systems, but letting God’s word once again become the standard of life.

Walls can protect a city, but God’s truth can renew a heart. If people have only outward religious activity without inward change of life, they still easily stray from God. When we are willing to humbly listen, understand, and obey the Bible, we can turn from the human mindset to God’s mindset and let Jesus be King in life.

When the people heard the words of the law, they wept because they knew their transgressions. God’s word is like a mirror, letting people see the problems in their lives and leading them to turn back to God. True repentance is not only grieving over past mistakes, but being willing to lay down pride and let truth change our lives.

A self-centered life easily defends itself and covers up problems; a humble life is willing to receive God’s light and admit its limits and transgressions. Yet God’s heart is not for people to stay in sorrow, but to be strengthened again through his mercy. When we no longer center on ourselves but trust God’s grace, we can move from confession to renewal, and from sorrow to hope.

Finally, Nehemiah and Ezra encouraged the people not to grieve, for “the joy of the LORD is your strength,” and told them to share food with those who had none. True joy is not that life has no difficulty, but that we know God’s grace and are willing to obey his will.

This joy is not a passing emotion, but a strength that comes from God and makes people stand again. When we take the Bible as our Standard and the Holy Spirit as our Guide and let Jesus be King, life turns from self-centeredness to loving God and loving people. True revival brings not only personal joy, but makes us willing to care for those in need and build relationships of mutual love, so that all glory goes to God.
a: Hunger for truth and understand the Bible earnestly
Set aside time to read the Bible every day, not only knowing what the text says but understanding its meaning and obeying God’s word.
Repent humbly and let truth renew your life
When God’s word shines on your problems, do not cover up or defend, but be willing to lay yourself down and receive God’s change.
Rejoice in the Lord and be a blessing to others
Do not stay in self-blame and sorrow. Receive God’s grace and joy, and take the initiative to care for, share with, and help those in need.
q: When I read the Bible, do I only want to increase knowledge, or do I truly want God’s word to shine on and change my life? When truth points out my problem, do I defend myself, or humbly repent and be strengthened again by the Lord?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving the precious Bible, so that I can know Your truth and will. Give me a heart that hungers for truth, so that I not only read and listen, but understand and obey Your word. When Your truth shines on my pride, self-centeredness, and transgressions, help me humbly repent and stop defending myself. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus live in me and be King in me. Holy Spirit, renew my life. Help me receive the joy and strength that come from You, live out the love of Christ, care for those in need, and build relationships of unity, giving all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will hunger for God’s word, understand truth, repent humbly, and obey his will, for the joy of the LORD is my strength!

t: Though Your Soul Is Downcast, Still Hope in God
v: As the deer pants for the water brooks,
My soul thirsts for God, for the living God.
My tears have been my food day and night,
These things I remember, and pour out my soul within me,
Why are you in despair, my soul?
b: The psalmist said, “As the deer pants for the water brooks, so my soul pants after you, God.” This is a beautiful and profound picture. A deer longs for streams of water in a drought, just as the human soul longs for the living God. The deepest need of a person’s life is not owning more things, but a close relationship with the God who created life.

People often fill the emptiness in their hearts with wealth, achievement, entertainment, and others’ approval, only to find that the more they gain, the less truly satisfied they are. This is because God created us to have fellowship with him. When we no longer center on ourselves but let Jesus be King, we can turn from pursuing the world to longing for God, and find true satisfaction in his presence.

The psalmist then described his pain: “My tears have been my food day and night.” Not only did he go through sorrow, but he was also mocked by others: “Where is your God?” Remembering the joy of worshiping with the crowd in the past made him feel loss even more. True faith is not never having tears, but still longing to draw near to God when we weep.

Those who trust in God also feel sad and lonely, and may even feel that God seems far away. God does not ask us to pretend to be strong, but invites us to come before him with our real feelings. When we no longer look only at our own pain, others’ words, and present circumstances, but turn our focus to Jesus, we can keep seeking him in weakness.

Finally, the psalmist said to his own soul, “Why are you downcast, my soul? Why are you disturbed within me? Hope in God!” True victory is not that sorrow disappears at once, but that in sorrow we still choose to hope in God and believe in his love and faithfulness.

The psalmist did not deny his emotions, yet he did not let emotions become the master of his life. He reminded himself that God is still worthy of trust and that he will yet praise him. This is turning from the viewpoint of circumstances to the viewpoint of faith, and from temporary pain to eternal hope. When we take the Bible as our Standard and the Holy Spirit as our Guide and let Jesus be King in our hearts, we can be strengthened again in sorrow and live a life full of hope.
a: Long for God more than for the world
Set aside time every day to draw near to God, so that prayer, Bible reading, and worship become a true need of your life.
In sorrow, pour out your heart honestly to God
You need not hide your tears and weakness. Bring the pain in your heart to God and seek his comfort and guidance.
Shift your focus and choose to hope in God
Do not let emotions, others’ criticism, or circumstances rule your life, but believe in God’s faithfulness and keep praising him.
q: When I feel downcast, lonely, or disappointed, what do I usually use to fill the emptiness in my heart? Am I willing, like the psalmist, to turn my focus from myself and my circumstances to God, and let him be my true satisfaction and hope?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for being the living God and the true satisfaction of my life. Give me a heart that longs for You, like a deer panting for the water brooks, longing to draw near to You every day. When I am downcast, lonely, weeping, or misunderstood, comfort me, so that I am not ruled by emotions and circumstances, but look to You alone. I am willing to lay down my pride and worry and let Jesus live in me and be King in me. Holy Spirit, guide my heart. Strengthen me again in weakness, keep me full of hope in difficulty, and help me love You, trust You, and praise You all my life, giving all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: My soul pants for the living God, like the deer for the water brooks! Though my heart is downcast, I will still hope in God, for he is my help, and I will yet praise him!

t: Live as a Child of God and Become Like Christ
v: See how great a love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God! For this cause the world doesn’t know us, because it didn’t know him.
Beloved, now we are children of God. It is not yet revealed what we will be; but we know that when he is revealed, we will be like him, for we will see him just as he is.
Everyone who has this hope set on him purifies himself, even as he is pure.
Everyone who sins also commits lawlessness. Sin is lawlessness.
You know that he was revealed to take away our sins, and no sin is in him.
Whoever remains in him doesn’t sin. Whoever sins hasn’t seen him and doesn’t know him.
Little children, let no one lead you astray. He who does righteousness is righteous, even as he is righteous.
He who sins is of the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the beginning. To this end the Son of God was revealed: that he might destroy the works of the devil.
Whoever is born of God doesn’t commit sin, because his seed remains in him, and he can’t sin, because he is born of God.
b: The apostle John marveled, “See how great a love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God! Such we are.” The greatest grace of the gospel is not only that sins are forgiven, but that by believing in Jesus Christ we are born again as children of God.

People often measure their worth by wealth, status, ability, and achievement, but the truly precious identity is belonging to the Father and having an eternal life relationship with him. We become God’s children not because we are good enough, but because of the Father’s love and Christ’s redemption. When we know this new identity, we no longer need to exalt ourselves or prove ourselves, but humbly give thanks, let Jesus be King in life, and live out the likeness of the Father’s children.

John went on to declare that when the Lord Jesus appears, we will be like him, for we will see him just as he is. Everyone who has this hope purifies himself, even as he is pure. True eternal hope is not only looking forward to being with the Lord in the future, but beginning today to pursue holiness and live out the life of Christ.

God saves us not only so that we may enter heaven in the future, but so that our present lives are gradually renewed. The life of the old self centers on itself, follows selfish desire, and wants to be king; the new life is willing to deny self and let Christ live within. When we turn from the earthly viewpoint to the eternal one, and take Jesus as our Role Model, the Bible as our Standard, and the Holy Spirit as our Guide, we become more and more like Jesus in daily life.

Finally, John solemnly pointed out that the Son of God was revealed to take away sins and to destroy the works of the devil. True new birth is not only confessing with our mouths that we are Christians, but a life that no longer makes sin its habit and is willing to do God’s righteousness.

John is not saying that God’s children will never stumble in this life, but stressing that one who is truly born of God cannot be at ease in sin or continue making rebellion against God a way of life. When we stumble, we should confess and repent, and rely on Christ’s forgiveness and the Holy Spirit’s power to stand again. Selflessness is not becoming perfect by our own effort, but laying down our own sovereignty and letting Jesus be King, so that the new life God has given keeps growing, living out holiness, righteousness, and love, and giving all glory to God.
a: Know your identity and live out the dignity of God’s child
Do not measure your worth by earthly achievements, but, because of the Father’s love, live out a life that belongs to God with thanksgiving.
Look to the Lord’s return and pursue a holy life
Do not only look forward to being with Christ in the future, but examine yourself every day and, by the Spirit, remove pride and selfish desire.
Refuse sin and let Jesus be King
Do not compromise with sin, and do not despair when you stumble. Be willing to confess and repent, and let Christ’s life be shown within you.
q: Do I truly know that I am a child of God? In daily life, do I still let the selfish desire and self-centeredness of the old self be king, or am I willing to purify myself by the Spirit and live a life that fits the identity of God’s child, preparing to welcome Jesus’ return?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving such great love, so that by believing in Jesus Christ I am born again as Your child. Free me from being bound by earthly achievement, status, and self-centeredness, and help me treasure the precious identity of a child of God. I am willing to lay down pride and selfish desire and let Jesus live in me and be King in me. Holy Spirit, guide me to walk on the path of holiness. When I am weak and stumble, help me repent humbly and rely again on Christ’s salvation. May I live out righteousness, holiness, and love every day, become more and more like Jesus, and prepare to welcome the Lord’s return, giving all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I am a child of God, loved by the Father and born again! I will abide in Christ, stay away from sin, live out holiness, and be fully like him when the Lord returns!

t: Be Alert in Disaster and Turn Back to God
v: The LORD’s word that came to Joel, the son of Pethuel.
Hear this, you elders,
Tell your children about it,
For a nation has come up on my land, strong, and without number.
He has laid my vine waste,
Mourn like a virgin dressed in sackcloth
The meal offering and the drink offering are cut off from the LORD’s house.
The field is laid waste.
Be confounded, you farmers!
The vine has dried up, and the fig tree withered—
b: The prophet Joel faced an unprecedented plague of locusts. He called the whole nation to listen and to tell the story to their children and to the generations that followed. True wisdom is not only knowing what happened in a disaster, but learning in it to fear God and understanding how life should turn back.

When life goes smoothly, people easily think they can control everything, but in a sudden disaster they find their own limits. Through the prophet, God called the people to be alert, not only to see the outward loss, but to think about their relationship with God. Today we also need to lay down pride, no longer treat ourselves as the master of our lives, but humbly seek God and let his truth renew our mindset and life.

The locusts devoured the vines, the fig trees, and the crops of the field, so that the people lost food and income, and even the grain offering and drink offering at the temple were cut off. Disaster lets us see that the wealth and security of the earth can all be lost, and only God is the true reliance of life.

When familiar life suddenly collapses, people easily fall into fear, complaint, and despair. Yet the Bible does not teach us to treat every disaster as retribution for personal sin, but reminds us to examine ourselves humbly in suffering and seek God anew. When we no longer care only about our own losses but turn our focus to God, we can learn to trust him in difficulty, let Jesus be King, and not be controlled by circumstances.

Finally, Joel described all the trees of the field withered and the joy of the people gone. This is not only an agricultural disaster, but a crisis of the whole society and of faith life. True revival is not only restoring outward prosperity, but letting hearts turn back to God and life be restored in relationship with him.

God called the people to mourn not so that they would live in sorrow forever, but to prepare them to repent humbly and seek his mercy. Today we also need to see, behind outward problems, the needs of inner life. First change the mindset, then life and living; when we take the Bible as our Standard and the Holy Spirit as our Guide, lay down the self-centered life, and let Jesus be King, we can move from desolation to renewal and become vessels of God’s work of revival.
a: Be alert in difficulty and examine yourself humbly
Do not only care about how to solve the present problem, but seek God’s will and think about what in your life needs to change.
Lay down self-reliance and trust God again
Do not take wealth, ability, and achievement as life’s greatest security, but let Jesus be King and rely on God alone.
Pass on spiritual lessons and bring revival of life
Share with the next generation what you have experienced of God in difficulty, and help your family and spiritual companions fear God and obey truth together.
q: When life meets sudden difficulty and loss, do I only want to get back to my former life quickly, or am I willing to humbly seek God and let him shine on me and renew my life through truth?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for reminding me through the Bible that everything on earth may change, and only You are forever faithful and reliable. When I face difficulty, loss, and desolation of life, keep me from being ruled by fear and complaint, and help me come humbly before You and seek Your will. Shine Your light on the pride, self-centeredness, and wrong reliance within me, so that I am willing to truly repent. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus live in me and be King in me. Holy Spirit, guide my life. Help me learn trust in hardship and hold on to hope in desolation, and pass the faith that fears God to the next generation, living out the life of Christ, giving all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will be alert in difficulty, look to God in desolation, lay down my own reliance, humbly turn back to the Lord, let Jesus be King, and live a renewed life!

t: God’s Promise Is an Anchor for the Soul
v: For when God made a promise to Abraham, since he could swear by no one greater, he swore by himself,
saying, “Surely blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply you.”
Thus, having patiently endured, he obtained the promise.
For men indeed swear by a greater one, and in every dispute of theirs the oath is final for confirmation.
In this way God, being determined to show more abundantly to the heirs of the promise the immutability of his counsel, interposed with an oath,
that by two immutable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we may have a strong encouragement, who have fled for refuge to take hold of the hope set before us.
This hope we have as an anchor of the soul, a hope both sure and steadfast and entering into that which is within the veil,
where as a forerunner Jesus entered for us, having become a high priest forever after the order of Melchizedek.
b: God promised Abraham that he would bless him and multiply his offspring. Yet from receiving the promise to seeing it fulfilled, Abraham went through a long wait. The Bible says, “Having patiently endured, he obtained the promise.” True faith is not demanding that God fulfill my wish at once, but believing God’s promise and staying faithful while waiting.

People often hope everything will go by their own timetable, and when there is delay they easily become anxious and doubtful, and even want to use their own methods to complete God’s work. Abraham’s experience reminds us that faith needs patience and patience needs trust. When we lay down our own sovereignty, no longer insist on our own time and methods, and let Jesus be King, we can learn to wait quietly and firmly believe in God’s faithfulness.

So that those who inherit the promise might be more sure that his purpose does not change, God not only gave the promise but swore by himself. Because God is faithful, he cannot lie. The foundation of our faith is not how firm our feelings are, but that God’s faithfulness never changes.

People’s emotions fluctuate, circumstances change, and ability has limits, but God’s nature and his promise are always reliable. When we build our security on ourselves, others, or circumstances, we easily worry about gains and losses; when we take the Bible as our Standard and the Holy Spirit as our Guide and turn our focus to God, we can hold on to faith in uncertain circumstances. True peace is not controlling the future, but trusting the God who holds the future.

Finally, Hebrews uses a vivid picture to describe hope: “This hope we have as an anchor of the soul, a hope both sure and steadfast.” What truly keeps life from being swept away by the storm is not outward stability, but our hope firmly joined to Jesus Christ.

An anchor keeps a ship from drifting in the storm; Jesus is the always-reliable security of our souls. As our eternal high priest, he has entered behind the veil for us, so that through him we can draw near to God. Selflessness is not losing what we rely on, but laying down the limited self and relying completely on the limitless Christ. When we let Jesus live and be King within, we can stand firm in hardship, hold on to eternal hope, and give all glory to God.
a: Believe the promise and learn patient endurance
Do not lose heart because God has not yet fulfilled things as you expected. Trust his faithfulness and wait patiently for his leading.
Lay down control and rely on God alone
Do not let emotions and circumstances decide your faith. Make God’s unchanging word the foundation of your life.
Take Jesus as your anchor and hold on to eternal hope
In the storms of life, do not only seek changed circumstances, but draw near to Christ and let him be the most secure protection of your life.
q: When God’s promise has not yet been fulfilled and life meets storms, am I quick to control the outcome by my own methods, or am I willing to lay myself down, endure patiently, and let Jesus be the anchor of my soul?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for being a faithful, covenant-keeping God who never changes. Your promises are true and reliable, and Your purpose never fails. When I face a long wait and the storms of life, take away my anxiety, doubt, and self-centeredness, so that I no longer rely on my own methods, but firmly believe Your word. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus live in me and be King in me. Holy Spirit, guide my life. Help me take Christ as the anchor of my soul, hold on to faith in hardship and be full of hope while waiting, until I complete the mission You have entrusted to me, giving all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: God’s promise never changes! I will endure patiently and trust firmly, take Jesus Christ as the anchor of my soul, and hold on to eternal hope!
